text.autoconfig.spatialhud.title: Spatial HUD
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideO: Imagine the selected lower HUD as a small sheet of paper resting on a waist-high lectern directly in front of you. It is intentionally hidden until you look down at it; it should not stretch up across your screen while you look level or upward. The Minimum Look-Down Angle controls when Spatial HUD starts doing work. Panel Positioning & Orientation controls where that paper sits and how it is tilted. The three methods below show the same selected HUD information in different ways.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideC: Method 1 — Green — Classic Affine: safest choice

Choose this when you want the best chance of compatibility with a large modpack. It uses Minecraft's normal HUD drawing path and moves the selected roots to the same physical lectern position. It still hides when you are not looking down. Its trade-off is important: Minecraft's normal HUD API can rotate and scale a group, but cannot squeeze every individual icon, letter, or slot into a true paper-shaped trapezoid. Green is the stable baseline, not the strongest perspective effect.
Method 2 — Blue — Captured Projective Mesh: real paper perspective

Choose this when you want the clear tapered-paper look. Spatial HUD first makes a private picture of only the selected lower HUD, then maps that picture across a dense mesh. Because every part of that picture shares one physical surface, the blue marker, backing, hotbar slots, icons, bars, and text all narrow together at the farther edge. It does not capture your inventory, chat, menus, minimap, debug text, or unrelated mod screens. This is the mode to compare against green when checking that the far/top edge actually tapers.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideW: Method 3 — Red — World-Space Texture: a real in-world panel

Choose this when you want the panel to exist as a real textured surface in the Minecraft world. It uses the same selected lower-HUD picture as blue Method 2, but puts it on a physical quad instead of a GUI-space mesh. That means normal game perspective handles the taper. You can decide whether it follows Camera Yaw or Player Body direction, and whether blocks hide it. It intentionally shows the last completed HUD picture, so a one-frame delay is normal; persistent flicker or missing texture is not.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.enable: Master switch for Spatial HUD. When disabled, every wrapped vanilla HUD root is immediately delegated back to Minecraft without a pose transform, private capture, or world-space draw. The separate Toggle Spatial HUD keybinding changes this same switch for quick comparison.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showPa: Draw the subtle translucent backing behind the selected lower-HUD strip. Methods 2 and 3 put this backing into the same private texture as the icons and text, so it receives exactly the same projective or world-space deformation. The small green, blue, or red method stripe remains as an identity marker even when this backing is hidden.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.onlyDu: Keep the spatial presentation out of inventories, chat, pause menus, Mod Menu, and other screens. This is recommended for normal play. Texture methods enforce the same screen-open boundary even if this option is turned off, because they intentionally capture gameplay HUD roots only.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.render: Choose the renderer, not the HUD contents. All three modes use the same physical waist-height lectern position and the same look-down threshold. Green Method 1 remains the stable native-HUD affine approximation, so it cannot taper each icon or glyph. Blue Method 2 genuinely projects every captured pixel across a tapered mesh. Red Method 3 draws that captured texture on a real world quad with optional terrain depth. No texture method captures screens, chat, maps, debug text, or unrelated mod GUIs.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.distan: Shared placement distance in block-like units, measured forward from the player-local panel origin. Methods 1 and 2 remain camera-yaw anchored while Method 3 uses the selected Method 3 anchor below. Increasing this makes the panel appear farther away and smaller in perspective; extremely low values are clamped to keep the plane in front of the camera.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeW: Physical width of the complete captured panel, including the hotbar and surrounding selected roots. The height is derived from the HUD capture envelope so aspect ratio stays intact. This is a geometric size control shared by all three methods, not a separate scale for each HUD element.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Move the panel sideways within its active horizontal anchor. Positive values move right and negative values move left. With Method 3 set to Camera Yaw, right and left follow the view; with Player Body, they follow the body heading instead.

Move the whole panel up or down relative to eye height. Negative values place it at waist height, as if it rests on a short lectern in front of you; positive values raise it. This changes position only—use the three rotation controls below to change the paper surface itself.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.minimu: Hard no-render threshold in camera-pitch degrees. At the default 30 degrees, Spatial HUD performs no private capture, mesh upload, or world-quad extraction while you look level or upward; the selected spatial HUD roots stay invisible until you deliberately look down toward the lectern. This is separate from natural physical off-screen clipping.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Primary Lectern Tilt — Left ↔ Right Axis

Rotate the panel around its own left-to-right axis. Positive values move the far/top edge farther away and make the blue mesh and red world quad taper more strongly. The 45 degree default is a moderate angled-paper lectern: it intentionally has visible far-edge narrowing at the 30 degree look-down threshold. This is a physical surface angle, not a camera-follow setting.
Fine Tilt Offset — Left ↔ Right Axis

Small additional rotation around the same left-to-right axis as Primary Lectern Tilt. Positive values push the far/top edge farther away; negative values pull it closer. Leave this at 0 unless fine-tuning the primary tilt, so the two controls do not unintentionally cancel each other.

Rotate the complete lectern around the player-local vertical up axis. Positive values turn its right edge farther forward and its left edge closer; negative values do the opposite. This is not camera yaw: it deliberately angles the paper left or right within the active horizontal anchor.

Rotate around the axis perpendicular to the paper surface. Positive values raise the right edge and lower the left edge; negative values reverse that slope. It is provided for deliberate three-axis adjustment, but 0 keeps text level and is the recommended normal-play value.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.worldS: Applies only to red Method 3. Camera Yaw keeps the physical plane in front while looking left or right, matching Methods 1 and 2. Player Body keeps it at body heading instead, so it can remain at the side while the camera looks elsewhere. This setting is ignored by Methods 1 and 2.

Applies only to red Method 3. When enabled, the HUD texture uses the world depth buffer, so terrain or a block between the camera and the plane hides it like a physical object. Disable it to retain the world-space position but draw the panel visibly through terrain. This setting is ignored by Methods 1 and 2.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.preser: Keep Companion Bars Native in Method 1

Compatibility safeguard for the green Classic Affine method. AppleSkin and Detail Armor Bar Reconstructed inject pixels inside vanilla status-bar extraction; leaving those complete roots native prevents detached or double-transformed companion pixels. Blue Method 2 and red Method 3 instead capture each selected complete root into one texture, so this safeguard is not used there.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHo: Include the hotbar plus the vanilla spectator menu and spectator tooltip in the spatial panel. Disable this if another HUD mod owns the hotbar or if you want Spatial HUD to present only the status information around it.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showBa: Include the main vanilla status-bar roots: armor, health, hunger, and air. In the two texture methods, decorations injected into those selected roots are captured with them; in Classic Affine, the compatibility setting above may keep companion roots native.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showXp: Include the vanilla experience progress bar, level number, and adjacent information-bar root. Disable it when another mod supplies a replacement experience display or when a cleaner hotbar-only panel is preferred.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showMo: Include the vanilla mount-health root while riding an entity. It has no effect while no mount-health HUD is active.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHe: Include the transient selected-item name above the lower HUD panel. Disable it if a tooltip or inventory mod already provides a preferred held-item label.
